rationale: bugs_open/266. A page whose pages.status='archived' is rebuilt and re-stamped build_status='deployed' + deployed_at=NOW() by at least FOUR independent producers, none of which reads pages.status. Live population verified at the artefact 2026-08-12: 5 pages serving HTTP 200 while archived, across 3 domains (fundamentallyai x2, leopardessconsulting x1, robot-hands x2); leopardessconsulting.co.uk/our-approach.html has been archived-and-serving since 2026-07-17. The load-bearing observation is that the producer named in the symptom is NOT the whole cause: for tool-llm-cost-calculator, ReconcileSitePlanAction behaved CORRECTLY -- it withheld the build and filed owned_page_review/needs_human_review, where it still sits uncompleted -- and image-build-handler rebuilt and deployed the same page sixteen minutes later through an unrelated path (needs_imagery -> image lands -> needs_page reason=image_landed). loadRealisedPages' missing status predicate (reconcile_site_plan_action.go:459-464) is real but is one of four doors, and it is the door that was already shut. So the fix is placed at the seam every producer converges on rather than in any producer. This blocks bugs_open/215's O2 remediation, which archives one side of seven duplicate page pairs: an archive that does not hold means that remediation silently undoes itself.

plan.summary: Two refusals for one state, plus a shared read. GitCommitAction refuses to commit an archived page (stops it SERVING); UpdatePageStatusAction refuses to stamp it deployed (stops the row CLAIMING a deploy that did not happen). Both go through one new reader, pageIsArchivedForGuard, which fails OPEN and reports whether it actually checked. No migration, no seed, no config key, no opt-in flag. Deliberately the OPPOSITE seam to the neighbouring owned-page guard (PBP-036), for a stated reason.

edits.rationale: One place any pipeline may read deploy-time archived status from, mirroring pageIsOwnedForGuard's contract exactly -- the reuse_agent seat objected to the neighbouring guard on precisely the ground of a second inline predicate, so this file exists rather than a SELECT status in two call sites. Returns (archived, checked): checked=false means the status could not be READ, not that the page is live, which is indistinguishable in the bool alone. Fails OPEN on any error, matching PBP-036's documented posture and for its reason -- failing closed would stop page deployment fleet-wide the first time the query hiccupped, which is worse than the harm prevented. resolveDeployTargetPage is a SUPERSET of resolveGuardedPage rather than a change to it: the deploy seam additionally sees the flat dispatch shape (page_id/site_id/page_name, and the input_data.-nested spelling a called agent receives) that page-rerender and section-editor actually arrive in. Widening the shared resolver itself would change what reaches the OWNED guard, and widening what reaches a function is a behaviour change to it even when the function is untouched (bugfix 149).

The seam every one of the four producers converges on, measured against live agent_definitions: page-rerender and section-editor each carry their own deploy_page->git_commit step, and page-build-handler's deploy_page is a call_agent to target_role page_renderer, i.e. into page-rerender's git_commit. Invisible to the many git_commit steps that deploy no page at all (CSS, JS snippets, RSS, reports, whole-site deploys), because resolveDeployTargetPage returns ok=false for them and the block is skipped entirely. Returns a SKIP rather than an error so one archived page cannot strand a whole batch -- the same choice PBP-036 made and for the same reason.

edits.symbol: UpdatePageStatusAction (new refusal, before the pageHasComponents block)
edits.rationale: Different damage from the commit guard, which is why both exist: without this, a refused commit still leaves build_status='deployed' and a fresh deployed_at, and that row is what every downstream selector reads. This action is the ONLY writer of pages.deployed_at in the estate (grep -rn "deployed_at = NOW()" --include=*.go platform/ internal/ returns this line and two sites writers). Asked of the DATABASE rather than of an upstream skip marker, because this guard's refusal travels through git_commit's output field rather than the assembly field upstreamAssemblySkipped reads. NO STATUS FLIP, unlike the shortfall guards below it which set needs_rebuild: queueing an archived page to be built again is precisely the loop being closed. Scoped to newStatus=='deployed' so ordinary bookkeeping on a retired page still writes.

Proven in BOTH directions rather than asserted: the refusal tests were run against a clean `git archive HEAD` overlay with the guard file added but the two wirings left out, which isolates the wiring as the load-bearing part. TestGitCommit_ArchivedPageIsRefusedBeforeCommit then fails with the archived page reaching 'no files to commit' (i.e. not refused), and TestUpdatePageStatus_ArchivedPageIsNotStampedDeployed fails with sqlmock reporting the unexpected UPDATE pages SET build_status=$2, deployed_at=NOW() firing with 'deployed' -- the defect itself, caught by the test. The negative ('it did not stamp') is enforced by registering NO expectation for the forbidden query, so an unexpected write is an error rather than an assumption. TestGitCommit_LivePageStillDeploys is the control WITHOUT WHICH a guard that refused everything would satisfy every other assertion in the file.

edits.rationale: Owner ruling 2026-07-28 condition 2: a platform seam is registered in the SAME commit that ships it, with its landmine and open review question written down. The landmine here is specifically that PBP-036's index line instructs the reader NOT to move a guard of this shape into git_commit -- correct for owned, wrong for archived -- so the two entries must cross-reference each other or the next reader will 'harmonise' them.

plan.risks: 1) FAIL-OPEN is a deliberate silent window: a page whose status read fails is committed without a check. Made countable via ARCHIVED_PAGE_GUARD_UNCHECKED rather than closed, matching PBP-036's answer to the same objection from the bug_historian seat. Failing closed would halt fleet-wide deployment on a transient DB error. 2) resolveDeployTargetPage runs one extra SELECT per page-scoped git_commit. Page-less commits (CSS/JS/RSS/whole-site) short-circuit before any query — pinned by TestGitCommit_NonPageCommitDoesNotTouchPages. 3) An archived page that SHOULD be live is now blocked until deliberately un-archived. That is the intent, and the refusal names the remedy in its own message, but it is live blocking behaviour on a shared seam. Known population is 5 pages across 3 domains; the two other lanes (leopardess, robot-hands) were told in their own handoffs per the 2026-07-29 consumers ruling, and nothing has been un-archived or retracted by this lane. 4) The guard reads pages.status, whose vocabulary overlaps build_status; 'deleted' is deliberately NOT annexed. 5) NOT an opt-in field: RFC_022/RFC_010's default-OFF rule governs new AUTHORITY on a shared seam, and this removes an authority nothing intended to have rather than adding one. Stated explicitly because the shape (new refusal on a shared seam) is close enough to that rule to be worth the reviewer's judgement.
